cohort: The study participants were 991 pregnant women from the Danish Fetal Origins 1988-89 cohort.
finding: Higher prenatal exposure to acrylamide, indicated by maternal HbAA levels, was significantly associated with an increased risk of clinician-based fetal growth restriction (FGR) and small-for-gestational-age (SGA), as well as a reduction in newborn size at birth (birth weight, head circumference, and length).
